questoes.enunciado: Identify the layer indicated by the double arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The epidermis is a stratified squamous, keratinized epithelium that consists of five strata beginning with the innermost, stratum basale, and ending with the most superficial, stratum corneum.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the layer indicated by the double arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The dermis, the connective tissue component of skin, consists of the reticular and papillary layers. The dermis lies between the epidermis and the hypodermis (which is not a subdivision of the skin).

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structures indicated in these images.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. A sweat gland is a simple, coiled tubular gland. Its long straight duct extends from the epidermis to the lower portion of the dermis or upper portion of the hypodermis where it connects to the coiled, secretory portion of the gland. The duct generally stains more intensely than the glandular portion and its distal end often coils with the secretory portion.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structures indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Dermal papillae are elevations of the papillary layer of the dermis that alternate with epidermal pegs, which are descending folds of the epidermis. The papillae are composed of loose connective tissue and may contain blood vessels or Meissner's corpuscles.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the layer indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The stratum corneum is the most superficial layer of the epidermis and consists of flattened, husk-like remnants of keratinocytes.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the layer indicated in these images.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The stratum spinosum, lying between the stratum basale and the stratum granulosum, gets its name from the spine-like processes which attach cells together by desmosomes.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the layer indicated by the double arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The stratum granulosum is 3-5 cells thick. The cells in this layer contain keratohyalin granules, which are intensely basophilic. This stratum lies between the stratum spinosum and the stratum lucidum.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structures indicated by the arrows in the electron micrograph.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. These electron dense granules contain highly phosphorylated proteins, which contribute to the matrix surrounding the tonofilaments in the stratum corneum. By light microscopy, these granules stain heavily with hematoxylin (basophilic).

questoes.enunciado: Identify the specific layer indicated by the double arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The papillary layer is the subdivision of the dermis just beneath the epidermis. It is composed of loose connective tissue which stains blue-green in this pentachrome-stained section.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the layer indicated by the rectangle in the image on the right.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The single row of cuboidal cells comprising stratum basale is the deepest layer of the epidermis and is the layer in which most of the mitotic activity of the keratinocytes occurs. These cells accumulate melanosomes produced by the adjacent melanocytes.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Melanocytes are most often found in the stratum basale and, to a lesser extent, in the stratum spinosum. These cells often show a clear cytoplasm. Melanocytes synthesize melanin, package it into melanosomes and then pass them into neighboring cells of the stratum basale.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the specific layer indicated by the double arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This deeper layer of the dermis, the reticular layer, consists of dense, irregular connective tissue and lies just beneath the papillary layer.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structures indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The reticular layer of the dermis consists of a dense, irregular connective tissue with thick bundles of collagen. Elastic and reticular fibers are both present, however, they are much smaller and fewer in number than the collagen bundles. In this toluidine blue stained section, the elastic fibers stain darkly.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. These sensory structures resemble cut onions due to the layers of perineurial cells which surround the central axon. Pacinian corpuscles are located in the hypodermis and respond to deep pressure.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Myoepithelial cells are octopus-shaped cells that lie just inside the basement membrane of the sweat gland. These cells contain contractile filaments; the contraction of myoepithelial cells aids in the expulsion of the secretory product of the gland.

questoes.enunciado: Name the protein that composes the structures indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This electron micrograph shows the stratum basale, consisting of a single layer of columnar cells. The cells contain tonofibrils which are bundles of tonofilaments composed of keratin filaments. The basal surfaces of these keratinocytes are highly folded for anchorage to the basal lamina.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The epithelium beneath the nail root is called the nail matrix and consists of stratum germinative and spinosum. It is a germinative zone, responsible for the production of new nail substance. More distally, the layer beneath the nail plate is referred to as the nail bed, which serves to anchor the nail plate to the underlying tissue.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The stratum corneum is the most superficial layer of the epidermis and consists of flattened, husk-like remnants of keratinocytes. In thin skin, seen here, the stratum corneum is thinner than that in thick skin.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the double arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Sebaceous glands are most often associated with hair follicles and, thus, do not occur in thick skin. These glands are simple branched acinar glands that secrete a thick oily material, sebum, onto the hair shaft, as well as distributing the sebum onto the skin surface via the hair follicles. Sebum is released by the holocrine mode of secretion.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Hair follicles have a terminal dilation called the hair bulb which surrounds a central papilla composed of dermal connective tissue. Within the papilla are numerous blood vessels necessary for survival of the follicle. Sebaceous glands (not seen in this image) are most often associated with hair follicles. Hair follicles are derived from the epidermis and are present only in thin skin.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: CORRECT.  The epidermis is a stratified squamous, keratinized epithelium that consists of five strata beginning with the innermost, stratum basale, and ending with the most superficial, stratum corneum.
